comparison: Perfect agreement on PEGylation methodology and characterization (C39-C47). Both evaluations find the peptide design and preparation well-supported. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this foundational work without raising concerns.

Complete agreement on RNA-seq data supporting NF-κB pathway involvement (C7, C90-C99). Both find the transcriptomic analysis compelling. OpenEval notes the limitation of using human BEAS-2B cells rather than mouse cells, which peer reviewers did not explicitly address.

Strong agreement on cytokine reduction data (C5, C55, C57-C58). Both evaluations find ELISA results compelling. OpenEval notes small sample sizes and requests explicit p-values, while peer reviewers found results 'compelling' without raising statistical concerns. Peer review also includes survival claims C53-C54.

Partial overlap on survival and biochemical markers (C48-C51, C53-C54). Both find the data supported. OpenEval specifically notes small sample sizes (n=5) and lack of explicit p-values, concerns not raised by peer reviewers who found the survival data compelling.

Strong agreement on histological evidence of tissue protection (C3, C59-C66). Both evaluations find the multi-organ, multi-staining approach compelling. OpenEval requests better description of semi-quantitative methods and blinding procedures, which peer reviewers did not address. Peer review encompasses broader tissue protection claims including C4, C67-C68.

Partial overlap on cellular viability and ROS data (C67-C68, C70-C71, C11, C35). Both find MTT and ROS measurements supportive. OpenEval cautions that C35 overstates ROS as the sole mechanism. Peer reviewers grouped these with broader tissue protection findings without noting mechanistic overstatement.

Complete agreement on neutrophil population data (C6, C73-C77). Both find flow cytometry evidence compelling. OpenEval notes the interesting observation about immature vs mature neutrophils (C148), while peer reviewers praised the immune cell analysis without detailed technical commentary.

Strong agreement on macrophage vs monocyte differential effects (C78-C81, C151-C152). Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval requests better explanation of biological significance, while peer reviewers incorporated this into broader praise of immune cell polarization work.

Complete agreement on M1/M2 macrophage polarization (C82-C87, C153, C155). Both find the flow cytometry data compelling. OpenEval notes that M2 increase is relative rather than absolute and requests mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers specifically praised the M1/M2 polarization findings as a key contribution.

Strong agreement on mitochondrial membrane integrity data (C8, C100-C103). Both find MitoTracker staining supportive. OpenEval notes the assay reflects both mass and membrane potential, suggesting JC-1 assays would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers found mitochondrial studies compelling without requesting additional assays.

Agreement on Drp1 phosphorylation and mitochondrial fission (C9, C104-C106). Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes the causal link to inflammation is inferred rather than demonstrated and suggests Drp1 inhibitor experiments. Peer reviewers praised the mitochondrial fission prevention without noting inferential limitations.

Strong agreement on Western blot time-course data for signaling pathways (C10, C107-C111, C164). Both find the temporal dynamics compelling. OpenEval requests densitometry quantification, while peer reviewers found the mechanistic evidence compelling without requesting quantification.

Agreement on qPCR data for macrophage markers (C12-C13, C113-C115). Both find results consistent with flow cytometry. OpenEval identifies a figure reference error (C113 cites Figure 2b incorrectly). Peer reviewers did not note this discrepancy.

Agreement on integrated mechanistic model (C112, C116, C163, C166, C169, C171-C172). Both support the NF-κB/mitochondrial dynamics mechanism. OpenEval notes causal relationships are largely correlative and requests direct mechanistic experiments. Peer reviewers praised the physiological mechanism elucidation without requesting additional causal validation.

Agreement on novelty claim (C166). Both evaluations support the novel mechanistic insights regarding PDZ inhibition of NF-κB affecting mitochondrial dynamics. OpenEval qualifies this as reasonable but needing more direct experiments, while peer reviewers described the research as 'highly regarded' and 'excellent.'

Significant disagreement on therapeutic candidacy claims (C14-C15, C38, C72, C120, C156, C175). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, citing major limitations: only prophylactic treatment tested, acute model only, no PK/toxicity data, uncertain translation. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAIN evaluation but with different emphasis: they note the proof-of-concept value while critiquing short duration focus and LPS vs live bacteria model. Both recognize limitations but OpenEval is more comprehensive in identifying translational gaps.

OpenEval evaluated background and rationale claims (C1-C2, C16-C27) as well-supported by citations. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these introductory/background claims, focusing instead on experimental results.
OpenEval evaluated immunological background claims (C28-C34, C143-C147) as appropriately supported by citations. Peer reviewers did not separately assess these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated PEGylation rationale and safety claims (C41-C43, C129-C133), noting that C133 ('no side-effects') is overstated without comprehensive toxicity studies. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these claims but noted model limitations in their overall assessment.
OpenEval evaluated mechanistic background claims (C52, C56, C69, C117, C160-C161, C165, C168, C170) as appropriately cited. Peer reviewers did not separately assess these literature context claims.

OpenEval evaluated limitation acknowledgments and future work proposals (C89, C127-C128, C134-C137, C141-C142, C158-C159, C174), noting appropriate qualification of speculative statements. Peer reviewers addressed limitations in their overall assessment but did not evaluate these specific discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluated integrative discussion claims (C121-C126, C138-C140, C148-C150, C154, C157, C162, C167, C173), noting reasonable interpretations but some inferential leaps. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these synthetic discussion claims, though some overlap with experimental findings (C148, C157, C162, C167) was addressed in R4 and R7.
